$comment: Exported from the Figma file by `pnpm figma:export`; change it in Figma, then export again and run `pnpm gen`.

whenToUse: The page’s main action, Solid: “Run test”.
Stopping that action, Solid Negative: “Stop”.
Every other action, Soft: “Scan again”, “Check now”.
An action on a red surface, Soft Negative: an error Banner’s Dismiss.
whenNotToUse: Opening another view or an address: use Link.
An icon with no words: use Icon button.
Checking a field’s value, like Test: use the Text field’s action.

builtIn: A focus ring, drawn as the Focus state.
Disabled and loading stay reachable by keyboard, so a tooltip can say why.
The icon and spinner are decoration: only the words are read.
toHandle: A label that says what happens, like “Run test”.
On a disabled button, a tooltip that says why.

whenToUse: An action an icon says on its own, like Refresh.
A help button, with the hint in its tooltip.
An action where a chip is too heavy, Ghost: a Dialog’s close.
whenNotToUse: An action that needs words: use Button.
Several actions behind one icon: use Menu.
An item’s tile that opens it: use Icon tile.

builtIn: Its label shows as a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus.
The icon is decoration: the label is what’s read.
Disabled and loading stay reachable by keyboard.
toHandle: A label that says what happens, like “Close”: it’s also the tooltip.
An icon that means that action at a glance.
On a disabled button, a tooltip that says why.

whenToUse: Opening another view from a header or a line of text: “All hosts”.
An address outside the app: About’s Source link.
whenNotToUse: An action that changes something: use Button.
A whole row that opens a view: use List row or a Stretched link.
A whole card that opens a view: use a Card that opens.

builtIn: Focus looks like hover, accent and underline, so no ring is drawn.
An address outside the app gets an arrow and is announced as opening a new window.
toHandle: Words that name where it goes, like “All hosts”.
Where the words can’t say it, the fuller words for screen readers, noted on the design.

whenToUse: A few secondary actions on a row, like a service’s Edit and Remove.
A destructive action kept out of the way, its item Negative: Clear history.
whenNotToUse: The page’s main action: use Button.
One frequent action: use Icon button.

builtIn: Enter opens it, the arrows move through it and Escape closes it.
Focus returns to the kebab when it closes.
toHandle: A kebab label that names its subject: “Options for Google”.
Item labels that say what happens: Edit, Remove.

whenToUse: The list the kebab opens, holding its Menu items.
whenNotToUse: A list that stays on the page: use Card list.

builtIn: Lines up under the kebab’s right edge.
Takes focus when it opens.
toHandle: Only Menu items, the most used first.

whenToUse: One action in the menu: Edit, Remove.
A destructive action, Tone Negative: Clear history.
whenNotToUse: A setting that stays on or off: use Toggle.

builtIn: Selecting it runs the action and closes the menu.
Its icon is decorative.
toHandle: A label that says what happens: Remove, not OK.

whenToUse: The kebab that opens a row’s or card’s menu.
whenNotToUse: One action on its own: use Icon button.

builtIn: Says whether its menu is open.
Enter or Space opens the menu on its first item.
toHandle: A name for what it acts on: “Options for Google”.

whenToUse: A short value to type, in a form so Enter submits it: a service’s Address or Name.
A value to check in place, with an action inside: Test.
whenNotToUse: Picking one of a few known options: use Segmented control.
A value to read, not edit: use Data row.
Submitting the form: use a Button outside the field.

builtIn: Its visible label is what’s read: no hidden name to write.
The feedback line is read with the field, and again when it changes.
Invalid is announced, not only shown in red.
toHandle: A visible label that names the value, like “Address”.
Sample input as the placeholder, never the only hint.
An error in words in the feedback line, so red isn’t the only cue.

whenToUse: Checking the field’s value in place: Test.
whenNotToUse: Submitting the form: use a Button outside the field.

builtIn: A real button inside the field’s border.
Loading, it stays focusable and keeps its name.
toHandle: A one-word label for what it does to the value: Test.

whenToUse: A setting that’s on or off, beside its title in a setting row: “Check for updates automatically”.
A change that applies at once, with no save.
whenNotToUse: Picking one of a few options: use Segmented control.
An action that runs once, like “Check now”: use Button.
A status the user can’t change: use Badge or Status dot.

builtIn: On and off differ in the thumb’s position, not colour alone.
Screen readers hear its label and whether it’s on.
Disabled stays reachable by keyboard, so a tooltip can say why.
toHandle: A label that repeats the setting’s title.
A description under the title, read with the switch.
On a disabled switch, a tooltip that says why.

whenToUse: Picking one of a few exclusive options, like Settings’ Theme.
A choice whose options all fit in view, each a word or two.
A choice that applies at once, with no save.
whenNotToUse: Turning one setting on or off: use Toggle.
Running an action: use Button.

builtIn: The thumb marks the chosen segment, not colour alone.
One Tab stop; the arrow keys choose.
Each segment is read by its label.
toHandle: A title for the group, on screen or noted on the design.
Labels of a word or two that make sense alone: Light, Dark, System.

whenToUse: A short task before going on: Add a service.
One thing up close: the Share Wi‑Fi QR code.
A prompt the user can put off: Update available.
whenNotToUse: A hint on hover or focus: use Tooltip.
A failure on the page: use Banner.
A few actions on one item: use Menu.

builtIn: Focus moves in, stays inside, and returns to what opened it.
Escape, the close button and Cancel all close it.
The page behind is dimmed and silent to screen readers.
Typed input survives a click on the backdrop, so a stray click loses nothing.
toHandle: A title that names the task: “Add a service”.
Where focus starts, when it’s a form: its first field.
A body that changes while open, marked to be read out: Share Wi‑Fi’s code.
Whether it can close while something runs: not when closing would abandon it.

whenToUse: Around every Dialog: it opens and closes it.
whenNotToUse: More detail on the page itself: use Collapsible.

builtIn: Draws nothing: the Dialog carries its role and focus.
toHandle: Nothing to draw: it has no layer in a design.

whenToUse: Why a control is off: “Connect to a network first”.
What a mark means: “Privacy-randomized MAC address”.
Detail that would crowd a row, like a host’s full name and IP.
whenNotToUse: Naming an icon-only button: use Icon button; its label is the tooltip.
A message the user must see: use Banner.
Anything to click: use Menu or Dialog.
A value that may be stale, like a rating while a new test runs: leave it off.

builtIn: Opens on keyboard focus as well as hover.
Its text is read as a description of what it points at.
Placed centred on its trigger, with no positioning by hand.
toHandle: A trigger that takes focus, like a button or icon, not plain text.
Over plain text, the hint also noted as screen-reader text.
A hint short enough for one line where possible.
Which side it opens on, clear of what it explains, noted on the design.

whenToUse: A word or two flagging a title: the ISP card’s VPN.
A card whose data updates live, Live badge in its header: Traffic.
whenNotToUse: A status beside its own words: use Status dot.
A failure the user should act on: use Banner.

builtIn: Capitals come from the style, so the words are read as typed.
Live badge’s dot is decoration.
toHandle: Words that carry the meaning without the colour.

whenToUse: A card whose numbers update live, in its header: Traffic.
whenNotToUse: A word or two flagging a title: use Badge.
A connection status: use Status dot.

builtIn: The pulsing dot is decorative.
toHandle: Words that say it’s live without the dot: Live.

whenToUse: A status in the words beside it: a device’s Online or Offline.
A live or busy state, pulsing: the title bar, a running scan.
whenNotToUse: A flag beside a title: use Badge.
Live data in a card header: use Live badge.

builtIn: Decoration: screen readers skip it.
Pulses in the app; drawn still here.
toHandle: Words beside it that say the status on their own.
Its pulse, noted on the design: Calm when steady, Live when streaming, Busy for work under way.

whenToUse: A wait inside a dialog: “Generating QR code…”.
A wait with more than one line: “Looking for your network…”.
whenNotToUse: A page’s first load: use Loading state.
A button’s wait: set Button or Icon button to loading.
A wait inside a button: use Button spinner.

builtIn: Silent: screen readers skip it.
Animates in the app; drawn still here.
toHandle: Words for the wait beside it, read out as they appear: “Generating QR code…”.

whenToUse: A small wait in a card header: the speed test running.
A small wait in a card body: the home Devices card’s scan.
whenNotToUse: A button’s wait: set Button or Icon button to loading.
A page’s first load: use Loading state.
A wait in a dialog or page area: use Spinner.

builtIn: Decoration: screen readers skip it.
In its button’s text colour, so it suits any button.
Spins in the app; drawn still here.
toHandle: Outside a button, a name for the wait, noted on the design: “Running speed test”.

whenToUse: A page’s first load, in place of its content, under the header and any Banner.
whenNotToUse: A page loaded with nothing to show: use Empty state.
A load that failed: use Banner.
A wait inside a dialog: use Spinner.

builtIn: Its line is read out as it appears.
The spinner is decoration; the line speaks for it.
toHandle: A line naming what’s loading: “Scanning your network…”.

whenToUse: A failure above a page: a load, scan or action that didn’t work.
A line on what’s on screen now: “Showing the last scan.”
whenNotToUse: A page loaded with nothing to show: use Empty state.
A choice to make before going on: use Dialog.

builtIn: Read out as soon as it appears.
Dismiss and Retry are buttons, with their focus and busy states.
The icon is decoration; the title carries the message.
toHandle: A title that says what failed: “Couldn’t scan for devices”.
A line under it that says what to try.

whenToUse: A page with nothing to show yet: “No services yet”.
A page the user can fill, with an action for the step: Scan again.
A page waiting on the user, Locked: “Administrator access needed”.
whenNotToUse: A page still loading: use Loading state.
A load that failed: use Banner.
One missing value in a row: use No value.

builtIn: The title is a heading, so screen readers can jump to it.
The placeholder rows and lock are decoration.
toHandle: A title naming what’s empty: “No devices found”.
A note an action adds, marked to be read out: “Scan started”.

whenToUse: A line under the title on why it’s empty or what to do.
A note an action adds, under the actions.
whenNotToUse: A failure to load: use Banner.

builtIn: Read straight after the title.
toHandle: A note that appears after an action, marked to be announced.

whenToUse: Labelled facts in a card: “Gateway”, “Band”, “Link speed”.
Facts on several topics in one card: a list each, stacked with hairlines.
A fact with no value that keeps its row: No value in its place.
whenNotToUse: A card’s headline figure: use Readout.
Rows that open something: use List row.

builtIn: Each label and value is read as a pair.
A row with no value isn’t shown, so no label sits alone.
toHandle: Words for a value that isn’t text, like a meter’s rating, noted on the design.

whenToUse: Facts on several topics in one card, a list each.
Flush to the card’s sides, so its hairlines run edge to edge.
whenNotToUse: Facts on one topic: use one list of Data rows.

builtIn: The hairlines are decorative.
toHandle: Groups whose first rows say their topic.

whenToUse: One labelled fact in a list: Gateway.
A value that isn’t text: signal bars.
whenNotToUse: A row that opens something: use List row.
A card’s headline figure: use Readout.

builtIn: Label and value are read as a pair.
A row with no value isn’t shown, so no label is read alone.
toHandle: Words for a value that isn’t text, like signal bars.

whenToUse: Where a value would be but there’s none, in place of a dash or “N/A”: not measured, unknown.
A value the app can’t format.
whenNotToUse: A field that may not apply: use Data row, leaving it out.
A section with nothing to show: use Empty state.
A page still loading: use Loading state.

builtIn: Read as its label, like “Not measured”, never as a dash.
toHandle: A label that says why: “Not measured”, “Unknown”.
A label nearby, like a row’s, that says what’s missing.

whenToUse: A headline figure and its unit: live speed, data used.
Labelled pairs side by side, sharing the row equally: Traffic’s “Download” and “Upload”.
A Home stat card’s figure, Compact and unlabelled.
whenNotToUse: A value in a list of facts: use Data row.
A number inside a line of text, easing each poll: use Metric value.

builtIn: The label and figure are read as a pair.
While the figure counts up, the digits can be silenced and the settled value read once.
toHandle: Figures side by side as one group, each with a label.
Without a label, a title nearby that says what the figure is.
The settled value to read while it counts, noted on the design: “182 Mbps”.

whenToUse: A number that changes each poll: latency, packet loss.
A value with a healthy range, in its status colour: latency.
A number inside text that sets its size: a data row’s value.
whenNotToUse: A headline figure with its unit and label: use Readout.
A value that never changes: use Data row’s plain value.

builtIn: Snaps to each new value when reduced motion is on.
The number shown is the number read.
A missing value shows No value, read as “None”.
toHandle: A label beside it that says what it measures.
The status in words where it matters, not only colour.
Which changes are worth reading out, noted on the design.

whenToUse: Signal strength or a rating, at a glance.
A level in its status colour, taken from the text around it.
A rating not measured yet: every bar unlit.
whenNotToUse: An exact figure: use Metric value or Readout.
Comparing traffic between rows: use Split bar.

builtIn: The bars take the colour of the text around them.
Unlit bars are a faint tint of the lit colour, not another hue.
A picture only: screen readers skip it.
toHandle: The rating in words, shown beside it or noted for screen readers: “Excellent”.
A colour with 3:1 contrast against the surface.

whenToUse: Download and upload in proportion, in a usage row.
Rows compared with each other, every bar scaled to the busiest row.
whenNotToUse: A rating or signal: use Bar meter.
A single headline amount: use Readout.

builtIn: Read as one image, named by its label.
toHandle: A label that says both amounts, down then up.
Figures beside it: colour alone doesn’t say which segment is which.

whenToUse: A card’s row that opens a view, an Icon tile first if the item has one: a capability, “About Rove”.
whenNotToUse: A label and value that open nothing: use Data row.
A whole card that opens: use a linked Card.
A row holding a bar or other block content: use Stretched link.

builtIn: The whole row is one button, read by its text.
The chevron is decoration.
Disabled, it stays reachable and is announced as unavailable.
toHandle: Rows that belong together grouped as one list.
A rating in words, not colour alone: “Excellent”, in its level’s colour.

whenToUse: The icon that starts an item’s row: a device, a capability.
A tile that opens something on its own, as the button version: Home’s capability strip.
whenNotToUse: An icon-only action: use Icon button.
A whole row that opens something: use List row, the tile inside.
An event on a timeline: use Timeline node.

builtIn: The plain tile is decoration: its icon isn’t read.
The button version is read by its label, and stays reachable when disabled.
toHandle: Words beside a plain tile that say what the item is.
A label for the button version with the item and its state: “Video calls: Good”.

whenToUse: A tile that opens something on its own: Home’s capability strip.
whenNotToUse: A whole row that opens something: use List row, the Icon tile inside.
An icon-only action: use Icon button.

builtIn: A real button, with hover and focus states.
Disabled, it stays focusable but ignores presses.
toHandle: A name with the item and its state: “Video calls: Good”.

whenToUse: One event in a timeline: “Device left the network”, “Service went down”.
A day’s events in a feed, one node each under its heading.
whenNotToUse: An item that isn’t an event: use Icon tile in its row.
A message about the whole page: use Banner.

builtIn: Nodes are read as a list, so screen readers count them.
The marker is decoration; the lines carry the event.
toHandle: Lines that say what happened, not only colour or icon.
When it happened, in its lines.
A day’s nodes under that day’s heading.

whenToUse: Related facts or settings under one title, like DNS or Updates.
A Home summary that opens its page: Usage.
A list that is one card, as a Card list: the tracked services.
whenNotToUse: An error about the whole page: use Banner.
Nothing to list yet: use Empty state.
A row in a card that opens a page: use List row.

builtIn: A card with a header is a region named by its title.
An openable card is one link, first in Tab order.
A card list is read as a list.
toHandle: A header on each card, so it has a name.
For an openable card whose title doesn’t say what it shows, a link label noted on the design.

whenToUse: A card’s content, under its Card header.
Settings or list rows, Body layout Rows: Updates.
A Data list stack, Body layout Flush, so its hairlines run edge to edge.
whenNotToUse: A footnote or status under the content: use the Card footer.

builtIn: Adds nothing for screen readers to read.
toHandle: Headings and lists inside it where the content has them.

whenToUse: A footnote under the body: the Router card’s packet-loss note.
The result of an action in the card: Settings’ update check.
whenNotToUse: Actions on the card: put them in the Card header.
A failure on the page: use Banner.

builtIn: Read last, after the body.
toHandle: A footer that appears after an action, marked to be announced.

whenToUse: The title row on top of a card: an icon, the title and its actions.
A badge or control at the row’s end: Live badge.
whenNotToUse: A page’s title and actions: use Page header.

builtIn: Its title names the card for screen readers.
Its icon is decorative.
toHandle: A short title that names the card: DNS.

whenToUse: A list that is one card: the tracked services.
whenNotToUse: Rows under a card’s title: use a Card with Body layout Rows.
Labelled facts: use Data rows.

builtIn: Read as a list, with a name.
Arrow keys move between the rows.
toHandle: A name for the list: Tracked services.
Rows that each stand alone.

whenToUse: Short facts on one line, like a device’s vendor and model, in place of a typed dot.
Facts that may be empty: they drop out with their dots.
Parts laid out by hand, a lone dot between them: the Services header.
whenNotToUse: Labels with their values: use Data row.
A status beside its words: use Status dot.
A missing value that should show: use No value.

builtIn: The dot is decoration: screen readers skip it.
A truncated item is still read in full.
toHandle: Items that read well in a row, without the dots.
The full value elsewhere when truncation can cut it off.

whenToUse: Short facts on one line that may be empty: a device’s vendor and model.
whenNotToUse: Parts you lay out yourself: use a bare Dot separator between them.

builtIn: Empty items drop out with their dots.
The dots are decorative.
toHandle: Items that read well in a row, without the dots.

whenToUse: The window’s top edge, once per window.
The connection in words, in the Title bar status: “Offline”, “No internet”.
A frameless window, with Window buttons.
whenNotToUse: A page’s title and actions: use Page header.
A status anywhere else: use a Status dot beside its words.

builtIn: The window buttons are named “Minimize” and “Close”.
The status is read out when it changes.
toHandle: The brand’s name as text, with the mark as decoration.
Status words that make sense heard alone: “No internet”.

whenToUse: The connection in a word or two, beside the brand: Online, No internet.
whenNotToUse: A status anywhere else: use a Status dot beside its words.

builtIn: A change is read out.
The dot is decorative.
toHandle: Words that make sense heard alone: No internet.

whenToUse: Minimise and close, at the end of a frameless window’s title bar.
whenNotToUse: An icon action anywhere else: use Icon button.

builtIn: Named Minimize or Close.
Skipped by Tab, like a native title bar’s.
toHandle: Nothing: the name comes with the action.

whenToUse: A page in the rail: Home, Devices.
An action at the rail’s foot: the theme switch.
whenNotToUse: An icon action outside the rail: use Icon button.

builtIn: Its name is also its tooltip.
The current page’s item is announced as current.
toHandle: One active item: the current page’s.
An action named for what it does: Switch to light mode.

whenToUse: The app’s pages, down the window’s left side, once.
Settings and the theme switch, at the bottom.
whenNotToUse: A page’s own actions: use Page header’s actions.
An icon action anywhere else: use Icon button.

builtIn: Each item’s label is its tooltip and what’s read.
The current page’s item is announced as current.
One Tab stop, on the current page’s item. Arrow keys move between items.
toHandle: A name for the rail: “Main navigation”.
Only the current page’s item active.
The theme item’s icon and label show where it switches: a sun and “Switch to light mode” in Dark.

whenToUse: The top of each tab’s page, like Devices or Usage.
A page over a tab, a back button in place of the icon: Hosts.
Something running on the page, in the status line: “Checking…”.
A page’s hint, in the info button: before the actions’ divider, never after it.
whenNotToUse: A card’s title: use Card header.
An error about the page: use Banner below it.

builtIn: The title is the page’s main heading.
A new status line is read out.
The back button is named “Back”, with a matching tooltip.
The info button is named, its hint in a tooltip.
toHandle: Labels and tooltips on the actions you add.
Status words that make sense heard alone.
